items.english_text: Katavasia: **"Magnify, O my soul, her who is more honorable and more glorious than the hosts on high. A strange and wonderful mystery"** (*Μυστήριον ξένον*); the Exapostilarion: **"Whom the multitude of the Prophets foretold"** (*Ἥν πάλαι προκατήγγειλεν*) thrice. At the Praises: the 4 Prosomoia: **"The lamp-bearing virgins"** (*Λαμπαδηφόροι Παρθένοι*); **"Glory"**; **"Both now and ever"**: **"Today she is led into the temple"** (*Σήμερον τῷ ναῷ προσάγεται*); the Great Doxology, and the Dismissal Troparion.[^178]

items.day_or_date: Sunday before the Nativity of Christ
items.slavonic_text: [English Facing Translation: Dec 26: Matins Concl. & Liturgy / Sunday after Nativity & St. Stephen (p. 275)]
items.english_text: Hypakoe recited plain; after the Sixth Ode, the Kontakion: **"He Who was begotten of the Father before the morning star"** (*Ὁ πρὸ Ἑωσφόρου Πατρὸς ἐκλάμψας*), the Ikos, and the Synaxarion of the Feast. The Katavasiai: **"He saved the people"** (*Ἔσωσε λαόν*); then the Ninth Ode of both Canons with their Megalynaria, and the Katavasia: **"Easier for us would it be"** (*Στέργειν μὲν ἡμᾶς*). The Exapostilarion: **"Our Savior, the Dayspring from on high, hath visited us"** (*Ἐπεσκέψατο ἡμᾶς*) thrice. At the Praises: the 4 Idiomela: **"Be glad, O ye righteous"** (*Εὐφραίνεσθε, δίκαιοι*); **"Glory"**: **"Today the invisible nature"** (*Σήμερον ἡ ἀόρατος φύσις*); **"Both now and ever"**: **"Today Christ is born in Bethlehem of the Virgin"** (*Σήμερον ὁ Χριστὸς*) up to the cue words **"and we cry aloud without ceasing: Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, good will among men."** (Note: the concluding phrase of the above Theotokion is sung by the choir as the opening proclamation of the Great Doxology); after which we sing the Dismissal Troparion: **"Thy Nativity, O Christ our God"** (*Ἡ γέννησίς σου*).

items.english_text: Hypakoe, the Anavathmoi of the Tone, and the Prokeimenon. The Canons of the Resurrection and of the Forefeast of that day. After the Third Ode: the Kathisma: **"Invisible God"** (*Ἀόρατε Θεέ*) once (see January 2); after the Sixth Ode: the Kontakion and Ikos of the Resurrection and the Menologion of the Saints of the day. The Katavasiai: **"He uncovered the bottom of the deep"** (*Βυθοῦ ἀνεκάλυψε πυθμένα*), and the entire order of the Morning Gospel; then **"More honorable than the Cherubim"** (*Τὴν τιμιωτέραν*). Exapostilaria: of the Resurrection and of the Forefeast: **"How shall river streams receive Thee"** (*Πῶς ῥεῖθρά σε ποτάμια*, see January 2). At the Praises: 4 Resurrectional Stichira and 4 of the Forefeast: **"O angelic hosts, go before"** (*Αἱ Ἀγγελικαὶ προπορεύεσθε δυνάμεις*); **"Glory"**: the Morning Eothinon Doxastikon; **"Both now and ever"**: **"Most blessed art thou, O Virgin Theotokos"** (*Ὑπερευλογημένη*); Great Doxology, and **"Today salvation"** (*Σήμερον σωτηρία*).

items.english_text: Ikos of the Triodion, the Menologion of the Saints, and the Synaxarion [Hypomnema] of the Sunday. The Katavasiai: on the 1st and 3rd Sundays, those of the Triodion; on the 2nd, 4th, or 5th Sunday: **"I shall open my mouth"** (*Ἀνοίξω τὸ στόμα μου*). Then we chant with verses "More honorable than the Cherubim"; Exapostilaria: of the Resurrection, of the Triodion, of the Saints, and the Theotokion. At the Praises: on the 1st and 3rd Sundays, we chant 2 hymns of the Resurrection, 3 of the Triodion, and 3 of the Martyrs; on the 2nd Sunday, after those of the Resurrection, we chant those of the Martyrs and then those of the Saint [St. Gregory Palamas] with the appropriate verses; on the 4th and 5th Sundays, we chant 5 hymns of the Resurrection and 3 of the Martyrs, with the following Verses at the last two: **"Wondrous is God in His Saints"** (*Θαυμαστὸς ὁ Θεὸς ἐν τοῖς Ἁγίοις αὐτοῦ*, Ps. 67:36 LXX) and **"In the saints that are in His earth, the Lord hath magnified all His good pleasure"** (*Τοῖς ἁγίοις τοῖς ἐν τῇ γῇ αὐτοῦ ἐθαυμάστωσεν ὁ Κύριος*, Ps. 15:3 LXX); "Glory...": of the Triodion; "Both now and ever...": **"Most blessed art thou, O Virgin Theotokos"** (*Ὑπερευλογημένη*); Great Doxology, and **"Today salvation is come unto the world"** (*Σήμερον σωτηρία*).
